chokepoints.name: Strait of Hormuz
chokepoints.between: Persian Gulf and Gulf of Oman
chokepoints.carries: About a fifth of global oil consumption and a fifth of LNG trade in normal years (EIA).

history.summary: The strait remained effectively closed pending Iranian conditions under the US naval blockade in force since 14 July 2026; a tanker was hit by an unattributed projectile on 4 October.

sources.name: Crisis Group: the future of the Strait of Hormuz

history.summary: An April 2026 ceasefire paused attacks on shipping after Iran hit vessels during the US–Israel war with Iran; it collapsed on 8 July.

sources.name: Crisis Group: the future of the Strait of Hormuz

chokepoints.name: Bab el-Mandeb
chokepoints.between: Red Sea and Gulf of Aden
chokepoints.carries: Oil and LNG between the Gulf and Europe, and all Suez-routed container traffic.

history.summary: Houthi strikes on Saudi-linked tankers from July 2026 and a declared blockade of Saudi Arabia cut transits by about a quarter; traffic stabilised at roughly 70% below pre-crisis levels.

sources.name: Lloyd's List Intelligence: Red Sea brief, 18 September 2026
Al Jazeera: Houthis deny plan to charge ships (Aug 2026)

history.summary: A US–Houthi ceasefire announced by Oman covered US ships only; most container lines kept routing around the Cape.

sources.name: Wikipedia: 2025 United States–Houthi ceasefire

history.summary: Houthi attacks on commercial shipping began with the seizure of the Galaxy Leader, diverting most Asia–Europe traffic around Africa.

sources.name: Wikipedia: Red Sea crisis

chokepoints.name: Suez Canal
chokepoints.carries: Around 12% of global trade before 2023; the shortest Asia–Europe route.

history.summary: August 2026 saw 1,232 transits, the busiest month since December 2023 but still 39% below pre-crisis levels, as MSC and COSCO began partial returns to the route.

sources.name: Lloyd's List Intelligence: Red Sea brief, 18 September 2026

history.summary: Transits roughly halved as carriers diverted around the Cape of Good Hope in response to Houthi attacks.

sources.name: Wikipedia: Red Sea crisis

chokepoints.name: Strait of Malacca
chokepoints.between: Indian Ocean and South China Sea
chokepoints.carries: The world's busiest oil chokepoint by volume, feeding China, Japan and South Korea (EIA).

history.summary: Open and heavily used; piracy and armed robbery in the Singapore Strait remain the main risk, not state action.

sources.name: EIA: World oil transit chokepoints

chokepoints.name: Taiwan Strait
chokepoints.between: East China Sea and South China Sea
chokepoints.carries: A large share of container traffic between North-East Asia and the rest of the world, and most of the world's advanced semiconductors by origin.

history.summary: Open; PLA combat-readiness patrols in May and live-fire drills off Fujian in July 2026 did not interrupt commercial traffic, and activity spiked again in mid-September.

sources.name: Al Jazeera: Taiwan monitors Chinese combat patrol (May 2026)
Taipei Times: defence report flags PLA landing capabilities (Sep 2026)

history.summary: Blockade-style PLA drills in late December 2025 briefly constrained shipping lanes around Taiwan.

sources.name: CFR Global Conflict Tracker

chokepoints.name: Turkish Straits (Bosporus and Dardanelles)
chokepoints.carries: Black Sea grain, Russian and Kazakh oil exports; governed by the 1936 Montreux Convention.

history.summary: Türkiye reaffirmed the Montreux Convention on its 90th anniversary: closed to Russian and Ukrainian warships since 2022, open to civilian traffic, with over 84,000 transits in 2025.

sources.name: Daily Sabah: Türkiye reiterates commitment to Montreux Convention
Carleton University: The Black Sea in 2026

history.summary: Russia terminated the Black Sea Grain Initiative; Ukraine opened a coastal corridor hugging Romanian and Bulgarian waters.

sources.name: Wikipedia: Black Sea Grain Initiative

chokepoints.name: Panama Canal
chokepoints.carries: About 5% of world maritime trade, including US Gulf LNG and grain to Asia.

history.summary: Drought cut daily transits to 32 from 15 September 2026 and lowered the draft to 14.48 m from 1 October, after rainfall 34% below average; FY2026 transits had been running 5% above the prior year.

sources.name: gCaptain: Panama Canal to cut daily transits as water outlook fades
Panama Canal Authority: monthly operations summary, June 2026

history.summary: Panama's Supreme Court annulled CK Hutchison's concession for the Balboa and Cristóbal terminals, and the state took control of the ports that US pressure had targeted since 2025.

sources.name: Baird Maritime: CK Hutchison ports sale to proceed without Panama terminals

chokepoints.name: GIUK gap
chokepoints.between: Greenland, Iceland and the United Kingdom
chokepoints.carries: The North Atlantic transit route for Russia's Northern Fleet submarines and transatlantic cables.

history.summary: Open; NATO maritime patrols and anti-submarine deployments have intensified since 2022, with Iceland and the UK hosting rotating P-8 patrols.

sources.name: Wikipedia: GIUK gap
